react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolome implicates one dominant pathway and one secondary pathway with high cross-paradigm confidence. Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00260) is the clear consensus winner across three independent paradigms: multi-DB ORA via RaMP-DB (FDR 1.27e-19, 8 input metabolites mapping to the pathway), KEGG-specific PSEA via MetaboAnalystR (raw p 2.12e-08, 6 hits), and m/z-direct network activity via Mummichog (rank 0, p 0.00227, 14 compounds from the network overlapping). The eight driver metabolites are glycine (C00037), L-threonine (C00188), L-cysteine (C00097), O-phospho-L-serine (C01005), S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine (C00021), L-cystathionine (C02291), guanidinoacetic acid (C00581), and adenosine 5'-monophosphate (C00020). Phosphoserine (C01005) is the key enzymatic pivot: it is synthesised from 3-phosphoglycerate via PHGDH (EC 1.1.1.95) and sits at the intersection of serine biosynthesis and the trans-sulfuration axis that feeds cysteine and cystathionine. Guanidinoacetic acid (C00581) links the pathway to creatine biosynthesis via arginine:glycine amidinotransferase (GATM). The parallel secondary signal in cysteine and methionine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00270) shares three metabolites with the primary pathway (L-cysteine, S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine, L-cystathionine), indicating that the trans-sulfuration pathway is co-activated. Niacinamide (C00153), N1-acetylspermidine (C00612), L-glutamic gamma-semialdehyde (C01165), and sulfate (C00059) contributed to additional peripheral hits including the urea cycle/amino-group metabolism (MUMM rank 1) and vitamin B3/nicotinamide metabolism (MUMM rank 4), but they did not reach the rank × score threshold required for inclusion in the two primary pathway claims.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolome implicates one dominant pathway and one secondary pathway with high cross-paradigm confidence. Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00260) is the clear consensus winner across three independent paradigms: multi-DB ORA via RaMP-DB (FDR 1.27e-19, 8 input metabolites mapping to the pathway), KEGG-specific PSEA via MetaboAnalystR (raw p 2.12e-08, 6 hits), and m/z-direct network activity via Mummichog (rank 0, p 0.00227, 14 compounds from the network overlapping). The eight driver metabolites are glycine (C00037), L-threonine (C00188), L-cysteine (C00097), O-phospho-L-serine (C01005), S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine (C00021), L-cystathionine (C02291), guanidinoacetic acid (C00581), and adenosine 5'-monophosphate (C00020). Phosphoserine (C01005) is the key enzymatic pivot: it is synthesised from 3-phosphoglycerate via PHGDH (EC 1.1.1.95) and sits at the intersection of serine biosynthesis and the trans-sulfuration axis that feeds cysteine and cystathionine. Guanidinoacetic acid (C00581) links the pathway to creatine biosynthesis via arginine:glycine amidinotransferase (GATM). The parallel secondary signal in cysteine and methionine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00270) shares three metabolites with the primary pathway (L-cysteine, S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine, L-cystathionine), indicating that the trans-sulfuration pathway is co-activated. Niacinamide (C00153), N1-acetylspermidine (C00612), L-glutamic gamma-semialdehyde (C01165), and sulfate (C00059) contributed to additional peripheral hits including the urea cycle/amino-group metabolism (MUMM rank 1) and vitamin B3/nicotinamide metabolism (MUMM rank 4), but they did not reach the rank × score threshold required for inclusion in the two primary pathway claims.
